messages.text: How do changes in Wi-Fi 7/8 technology affect the measurement capability required from Signaling / Non-signaling Tester?

Wi‑Fi 7 and Wi‑Fi 8 push testers from “basic WLAN RF TX/RX” toward **wideband, multi-link, low-EVM, low-latency, protocol-aware RF validation**.

### 1) Wider bandwidth and higher modulation raise RF quality requirements

Wi‑Fi 7 / 8 keep very demanding PHY parameters: the RS Knowledge evidence says Wi‑Fi 8 continues Wi‑Fi 7 core PHY parameters including **frequencies up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz, 4096QAM modulation, and MLO**. It also says Wi‑Fi 8 shifts focus from sheer speed to **ultra-high reliability**.  

**Impact on testers:**

| Technology change | Required tester capability |
|---|---|
| 320 MHz channels | RF generator/analyzer must support ≥320 MHz analysis/generation bandwidth with calibrated flatness, phase, and amplitude accuracy. |
| 4096QAM | Much lower residual EVM floor is required; tester EVM must be significantly better than DUT limits. |
| 6 GHz operation up to 7.125 GHz | RF front end, switching, cables, fixtures, and calibration must remain accurate across 2.4 / 5 / 6 GHz. |
| Higher throughput | Signaling tester must sustain real application/IP throughput and PER/throughput measurements, not only packet decode. |

Older WLAN test capability can become insufficient: the KB notes CMW500 WLAN bandwidth support up to **160 MHz** for 802.11ax-era testing, while Wi‑Fi 7/8 require up to **320 MHz**. The CMX500 evidence, by contrast, lists WLAN signaling and WLAN TX measurements including **802.11be and 802.11bn**, plus PER / throughput measurements and 2x2 MIMO support.

### 2) MLO changes signaling tester requirements more than classic RF testers

**Multi-Link Operation, MLO**, means the DUT may use multiple links across bands/channels simultaneously.

For a **signaling tester**, this requires:

- Emulating AP behavior across multiple links.
- Coordinating link setup, teardown, traffic steering, and link switching.
- Measuring per-link and aggregate throughput / PER.
- Testing latency and reliability when links are impaired differently.
- Supporting coexistence or desense scenarios when WLAN and cellular radios operate together.

For a **non-signaling tester**, MLO creates RF measurement needs such as:

- Multi-port or fast-switched measurements across multiple RF chains.
- Time alignment between links.
- Simultaneous or coordinated waveform generation / analysis.
- Per-link EVM, power, spectral mask, leakage, frequency error, and timing measurements.

### 3) Puncturing and flexible resource use require more detailed waveform analysis

Wi‑Fi 7 introduced puncturing concepts, and Wi‑Fi 8 adds further PHY complexity. The KB specifically identifies Wi‑Fi 8 testing hurdles such as **distributed resource units, dRU**, and **unequal modulation, UEQM**. It says dRU measurements verify whether a device can boost uplink transmit power and improve connection reliability, and UEQM analysis checks whether a device adapts modulation correctly for specified MCS combinations.

**Tester implications:**

- The analyzer must understand non-contiguous or distributed allocations, not just one continuous channel.
- EVM must be reported by subcarrier / RU / allocation, not only as one aggregate number.
- The tester must validate that the DUT applies the correct MCS and modulation per resource unit.
- Power spectral density and emissions need to be checked under partial-band and punctured-band operation.

### 4) Wi‑Fi 8 shifts emphasis from peak rate to reliability and latency

The evidence says Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn focuses on **ultra-high reliability, UHR**, while retaining Wi‑Fi 7-like bandwidth/modulation/MLO parameters.

That changes test priorities:

| From Wi‑Fi 7 focus | Toward Wi‑Fi 8 focus |
|---|---|
| Peak throughput | Reliability under interference and congestion |
| Single high-rate link | Multi-link robustness |
| Basic EVM / power / mask | EVM plus dRU / UEQM behavior |
| Packet success rate | Latency, jitter, failover, recovery time, consistent QoS |
| Ideal channel tests | Stress tests with impairments, fading, traffic load, coexistence |

So a signaling tester needs stronger **traffic, impairment, and protocol-control capability**, while a non-signaling tester needs more **waveform-aware RF analysis**.

### 5) Signaling vs. non-signaling: capability split

**Signaling tester / callbox needs:**

- Wi‑Fi 7 / 8 AP emulation.
- MLO connection control.
- PER, throughput, latency, and application traffic testing.
- RF TX measurements while the device is in realistic connected mode.
- Regression testing across 2.4 / 5 / 6 GHz, channel widths, MCS, and MIMO modes.
- Future Wi‑Fi 8 support for dRU and UEQM-style measurements.

The KB positions CMX500 as a **universal one-box network emulation and measurement solution** with WLAN signaling and TX measurements for **802.11be and 802.11bn**, plus PER / throughput measurement.

**Non-signaling tester needs:**

- 320 MHz waveform generation and analysis.
- Very low residual EVM for 4096QAM validation.
- Spectrum mask, power, frequency error, phase noise / impairments, and EVM analysis.
- Multi-DUT / multi-port efficiency for production.
- Analysis of punctured, distributed, and unequal-modulation waveforms.
- Calibration and de-embedding support for wideband 6 GHz measurements.

### Bottom line

Wi‑Fi 7/8 make WLAN testing much closer to high-end cellular-style testing:

- **Bandwidth doubles vs. many Wi‑Fi 6/6E test setups**: up to 320 MHz.
- **Modulation becomes more sensitive**: 4096QAM demands better EVM headroom.
- **MLO requires protocol-aware, multi-link signaling tests**.
- **Puncturing / dRU / UEQM require allocation-aware RF analysis**.
- **Wi‑Fi 8 adds reliability-focused validation**, not just higher data-rate checks.

So the required tester evolves from a WLAN packet/RF tester into a **wideband, low-EVM, multi-channel, multi-link signaling and RF measurement platform**.

Sources from RS Knowledge result: CMX500 product-positioning passages; CMW500 WLAN 160 MHz capability passage; “Rohde & Schwarz and Broadcom showcase first Wi‑Fi 8 RF signaling tests” passages covering Wi‑Fi 8 / 802.11bn, UHR, 320 MHz, 4096QAM, MLO, dRU and UEQM.

passages.text:
Rohde & Schwarz and Broadcom showcase first Wi-Fi 8 RF signaling tests, paving way for next-gen connectivity › 重點摘要
- 來源未標示發布日期；raw frontmatter `created: 2026-09-11`，本文 ingest 日期為 2026-09-15。
- [[Rohde & Schwarz]] 宣稱在最終 IEEE standard ratification 之前，已將 first [[Wi-Fi 8 RF signaling tests]] 實作到 [[R&S CMX500]] one-box signaling tester。
- 展示情境：[[MWC Barcelona 2026]]，[[Rohde & Schwarz]] booth 5A80，Fira Gran Via Barcelona，hall 5。
- 測試對象：[[Broadcom]] prototype next-generation WLAN device / prototype [[Wi-Fi 8]] device。
- [[Wi-Fi 8]] / [[IEEE 802.11bn]] 的焦點被描述為從 sheer speed 轉向 ultra-high reliability（[[UHR]]）performance。
- 來源稱 [[Wi-Fi 8]] 延續 [[Wi-Fi 7]] 的 core PHY parameters：supported frequencies up to 7.125 GHz、channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz、4096QAM modulation、[[MLO]]。
- 來源列出 [[Wi-Fi 8]] / [[IEEE 802.11bn]] 的新 testing hurdles，包括 [[distributed resource units]]（dRU）與 [[unequal modulation]]（UEQM）。
- dRU measurements 被描述為可驗證 device boosting uplink transmit power 與 improving connection reliability 的 effectiveness。
- UEQM analysis 被描述為可評估 test device 是否能依 specified modulation coding scheme（MCS）combinations 正確 adapt modulation。
- [[R&S CMX500]] 被定位為 modular、powerful one-box signaling tester，支援 [[LTE]]、[[NR]] SA/NSA、[[NR-NTN]]、[[NB-NTN]]、Direct-to-Cell（[[D2C]] / [[DTC]]）與 WLAN including [[Wi‑Fi 7]] and [[Wi‑Fi 8]]。
- Press & media contact：[[Christian Mokry]]，PR Manager Test & measurement。

| 項目 | 規格 |
|---|---|
| Connector | 3 × IF Out，port 1、port 2、port 3，SMA |
| Frequency range | 6 GHz to 20 GHz，inclusive modulation bandwidth |
| Frequency resolution | < 0.1 Hz |
| Frequency uncertainty | same as timebase + frequency resolution |
| Frequency settling time | < 300 µs |
| Maximum reverse power | 0 V DC、+25 dBm |
| Output level range | 6 GHz to 20 GHz，PEP，for best SNR/IMD performance：–20 dBm to +2 dBm；overrange up to +10 dBm |
| Output level resolution | 0.1 dB |
| Output level uncertainty | +15 °C to +35 °C、no overranging、within ±5 °C from last level alignment procedure temperature：6 GHz to 20 GHz < 1.5 dB；< 0.5 dB typ. |
| Output level repeatability | after 1 h warm-up time、same level and frequency、no temperature change、insignificant time change：< 0.1 dB |
| IF ports isolation | IF In x to IF Out y：–60 dB nom.；IF Out x to IF Out y：–30 dB nom. |
| Second harmonics attenuation | 6 GHz to 20 GHz：> 35 dB nom. |
| Third harmonics attenuation | 6 GHz to 20 GHz：> 45 dB nom. |

IF generator EVM 條件：5G NR PDSCH、channel bandwidth 100 MHz、full allocation、SCS 60 kHz / 120 kHz、modulation 64QAM、temperature +15 °C to +35 °C、within ±5 °C from last level alignment procedure temperature、PAR 11.8 dB。EVM 摘錄：6 GHz to 10 GHz、P –28 dBm to –10 dBm RMS：**< –40 dB meas.**；10 GHz to 14 GHz：**< –37 dB meas.**；14 GHz to 17 GHz、P –26 dBm to –10 dBm RMS：**< –37 dB meas.**。

Regulatory test for wireless devices with cellular technology › 重點摘要
- 來源將 wireless products 的 market access approval testing 分成三類：[[Regulatory Compliance Test]]、[[Telecom Industry Certification Test]]、[[Cellular Network Operator Acceptance Test]]。Regulatory compliance 被描述為各區域法律面 market access 的必要條件；industry certification 例子包含 [[GCF]] / Cellular、[[Bluetooth SIG]]、[[FiRa]] / [[UWB]]、[[Wi-Fi Alliance]]；operator acceptance test 例子包含 AT&T、VzW、T-mobile、CMCC。
- 來源主張 wireless products 需要 [[CE marking]] / [[FCC ID]]；test results 是 technical documentation 的一部分，需在產品投放市場前準備、可提供給 surveillance authorities，並自 placed on the market 起保存 10 years。
- 來源列出 Ericsson Mobility Visualizer Jan 2023 的 mobile subscriptions 表，顯示 2022–2028 的 5G subscriptions 由 1046.006 增至 4974.568；但單位與表格數值口徑未在轉檔文字中完整標示。
- [[CE RED 無線設備法規測試]]被整理成四類 essential requirements：Art 3.1a Health & Safety、Art 3.1b EMC、Art 3.2 Radio Spectrum、Art 3.3 Specific topics。來源列出多個 ETSI EN standards，例如 [[EN 300 328]]、[[EN 301 893]]、[[EN 303 687]]、[[EN 301 908-1]]、[[EN 301 908-13]]、[[EN 301 908-24]]、[[EN 301 908-25]]、[[EN 301 489-52]] 等。
- 對 [[5G NR SAR testing]]，來源指出 5G NR network emulator is required to drive EUT to extreme transmission condition，multi-radio UE 的 average-SAR feature 需要 flexible signaling functions，涵蓋 cellular standards、Wi-Fi 與 Bluetooth；來源將 [[R&S CMW500]] / [[R&S CMX500]] 稱為 SAR / HAC signaling solution。
- 對 Art 3.1b EMC，來源指出 EMC tests 需要 radio enabled 與 radio disabled conditions，因此 5G NR 也需要 signaling solution；mobile phone 仍需要 [[Audio Breakthrough]] test，從 GSM 到 VoLTE / VoNR by 5G。來源提到 [[R&S TS9982 EMS Test System]] 與 [[R&S TS9975 EMI Test System]]。
- 對 Art 3.2 Radio Spectrum，來源指出 5G NR specification 包含 FR1 與 FR2；FR1 test setup stays conducted，FR2 test setup becomes radiated；並把 3GPP test cases、CTIA-OTA test cases、TRP / TRS、RSE 測試連到 [[R&S TS8991]] 與 [[R&S TS8996]]。

依 [[CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100]]，[[R&S CMX500]] 是 universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution，支援最新 3GPP [[5G NR]] technology，適用於 device testing，涵蓋 [[LTE]]、[[NR FR1]]、[[NR FR2]]，並支援 non-standalone（NSA）、standalone（SA）、FDD 與 TDD。

answer.text:
### Signaling tester implications
A signaling tester must support Wi‑Fi 8 continuing Wi‑Fi 7 core PHY parameters: frequencies up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz, 4096QAM, and MLO [25].
Because Wi‑Fi 8 targets UHR, IEEE 802.11bn introduces new PHY and MAC technologies that create new testing hurdles, so signaling testers need enhanced Wi‑Fi 8 test capability beyond basic Wi‑Fi 7 PHY support [25].
In WLAN development, antenna, RF transmitter and RF receiver measurements must be done under real-world conditions in signaling mode, so the signaling tester must emulate realistic connections rather than only generate/analyze packets [27].
Since MLO is a key Wi‑Fi 7 feature, the signaling test environment must provide multiple RF chains [27].
The CMX500 is described as a multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester with integrated Wi‑Fi 7 functionality and newly added Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn testing capabilities, including validation of a Broadcom prototype Wi‑Fi 8 device and Wi‑Fi 8 physical-layer features [26][27].
Embedded IP test capability is relevant because Wi‑Fi 7-specific testing can include higher-layer behavior in addition to RF measurements [27].
### Non-signaling tester implications
In WLAN production, all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time, so production testers must prioritize fast RF measurement throughput rather than full connection emulation [28].
The non-signaling tester must cover Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and future Wi‑Fi 8-related waveforms up to 8 GHz, with bandwidths up to 500 MHz [28].
The CMP180 is positioned for this non-signaling production role and is described as able to verify a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode [28].
### Specific measurement-capability effects
| Topic | Required tester impact supported by RAW evidence |
|---|---|
| Bandwidth | Signaling must cover Wi‑Fi 7/8 core channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz; non-signaling production/R&D needs headroom up to 500 MHz and demonstrated 480 MHz WLAN waveform verification for possible Wi‑Fi 8 evolution [25][28]. |
| Modulation | Testers must support 4096QAM because Wi‑Fi 8 retains this Wi‑Fi 7 PHY parameter [25]. |
| MLO | Signaling test setups need multiple RF chains because MLO is a key Wi‑Fi 7 feature and is retained in Wi‑Fi 8 [25][27]. |
| RF performance | Signaling-mode development testing must measure antenna, RF transmitter and RF receiver characteristics under real-world conditions [27]. |
| Future Wi‑Fi 8 features | Wi‑Fi 8 introduces new PHY/MAC technologies for UHR that create new testing hurdles, and R&S/Broadcom will validate Wi‑Fi 8 physical-layer features on a prototype device [25][26]. |
| 480 MHz future waveform | A 480 MHz WLAN waveform is described as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 candidate, so testers with 500 MHz bandwidth support are positioned as future-proof for production and R&D [28]. |
【推論】For signaling testers, the practical change from Wi‑Fi 7 to Wi‑Fi 8 is not just higher peak speed support, because Wi‑Fi 8 keeps 320 MHz, 4096QAM and MLO but adds UHR-driven PHY/MAC testing hurdles; therefore, signaling testers need multi-channel, multiple-RF-chain, real-world RF and new Wi‑Fi 8 feature validation capability [25][26][27].
【推論】For non-signaling testers, the key change is bandwidth headroom and fast RF production measurement: although Wi‑Fi 8 retains 320 MHz in the cited core PHY parameters, a 480 MHz candidate waveform and 500 MHz tester bandwidth indicate a need to prepare for wider future waveform verification [25][28].

cited_passages.text: [Wi-Fi 8](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/solutions/wireless-communications-testing/wireless-standards/wlan-wi-fi/wi-fi-8-testing/wi-fi-8-testing_258504.html "Wi-Fi 8") builds upon the foundation of Wi-Fi 7, retaining core physical layer parameters like supported frequencies up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz and 4096QAM modulation, as well as Multi-Link-Operation (MLO). However, to achieve its UHR goals, IEEE 802.11bn introduces a suite of innovative PHY and MAC layer technologies that present new testing hurdles. At MWC 2026, visitors can experience how to address key testing challenges associated with Wi-Fi 8 with the enhanced testing capabilities of the CMX500 one-box signaling tester, one of the most versatile mobile device test platforms in the market, which supports many of the demanding features of Wi-Fi 7 and Wi-Fi 8 today.

cited_passages.text: During the development of WLAN devices, measurements of the antennas as well as RF transmitter and receiver characteristics must be conducted under real-world conditions in signaling mode. With MLO being a key feature in Wi-Fi 7, a test environment that provides multiple RF chains is crucial. The R&S CMX500 one-box tester from Rohde & Schwarz, featuring integrated Wi-Fi 7 test functionality, is a multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester. Its flexibility, support for multiple radio technologies, and embedded IP test capabilities make it a versatile solution for a broad range of Wi-Fi 7-specific tests.

cited_passages.text: In the production phase of WLAN devices, all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time. Rohde & Schwarz has optimized the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester for this purpose. The instrument supports many cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi-Fi 6E, Wi-Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz in frequency with bandwidths up to 500 MHz. Leveraging the wide bandwidth, the R&S CMP180 will demonstrate at MWC its ability to verify a WLAN waveform with 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) standard. This feature shows that the cost-effective instrument is future-proof for users not only in production, but also in R&D.
